title: Collections and a Progress Tracker
summary: Apply List, Map, Set, generics, iteration, immutable views, exceptions, and modular design in a progress-tracker capstone.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the Java behavior taught in Collections and a Progress Tracker
Compile, run, and test the behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Use `List` for ordered values, `Set` for uniqueness and membership, and `Map` for key-value relationships. Generic arguments such as `List<String>` preserve element types without casts. Choose an implementation according to behavior: `ArrayList`, `HashSet`, and `HashMap` are common defaults. A missing map key returns null from `get`, so distinguish absence with `containsKey` or use an intentional default. Do not structurally modify a collection during enhanced iteration. Return defensive copies or unmodifiable views when callers must not mutate internal state.
keyPoints: Use `List` for ordered values, `Set` for uniqueness and membership, and `Map` for key-value relationships.
